news.headline: AI-financing concern kept Asian equities under pressure while lower oil supported bonds and US futures
facts: Reuters reported Japan's Nikkei down 2.0% and South Korea down 1.6% in early Monday trade.
Five AI hyperscalers are expected by Goldman Sachs to raise combined capex to about US$1.2tn next year.
The US 10-year yield was down about 3bp to 5.0645%, while spot gold was up 0.4% at US$4,181/oz.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Negative immediate sentiment for high-duration AI server, foundry, packaging and component names; lower yields are a partial offset. The effect is valuation/financing-driven, not evidence of an end-demand collapse.
news.uncertainty: Canonical Reuters page was blocked to extraction; body facts above are limited to the checked search-result excerpt. Exact Reuters publication time was not exposed.

news.headline: Wall Street sold off Friday as AI infrastructure debt and oil risks hit technology
facts: Reuters syndication: S&P 500 -1.09% to 7,659.44, Nasdaq -2.15% to 26,140.03, Dow -0.34% to 52,002.41.
CoreWeave fell 12%; the PHLX chip index fell 3.8% for an eighth straight decline.
For the week, S&P 500 lost about 1.95% and Nasdaq 4.48%; oil rose more than 3% Friday on Middle East supply concern.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Bearish opening impulse for Taiwan semiconductors/AI supply chain, particularly richly valued server, power, cooling, optical and PCB names. Energy and utilities relative strength abroad is not a direct bullish Taiwan read-through.
news.uncertainty: Authorized Reuters syndication checked; article date exposed but exact publication time was not.

news.headline: Trump to use up to 60 days to review Russia sanctions after waiver
facts: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump would use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of Russia-related sanctions and tariffs waived a day earlier.
The waived Graham Act measures had been due to take effect the following week.
Rubio also defended a Russia-US diesel arrangement; Trump said initial supply would exceed 300,000 metric tons, followed by November shipments.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Potentially disinflationary if diesel supply actually rises, which would help bonds and rate-sensitive technology valuations. Execution and legal/political durability remain uncertain.
news.uncertainty: Reuters canonical page was blocked to extraction; claims are constrained to checked Reuters search excerpts. Waiver is not a permanent repeal and shipment execution was not independently verified.

news.headline: Japan approved TSMC's revised 3nm Kumamoto fab plan
facts: Japan's METI approved a revised second-fab plan for 3nm production, described as the first 3nm plant in Japan.
Reported first-stage capacity is 6,000 wafers/month versus 48,000 under the former 6nm/12nm plan.
Operations are scheduled for December 2028; final production depends on subsidy scale.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Structurally positive for TSMC demand visibility and geographic diversification, but possible long-run capex/cost dilution and domestic ecosystem migration should be monitored. Near-term Taiwan capacity is not displaced by a 2028 start.
news.uncertainty: Checked Taiwan News/CNA report attributed to METI and Japanese media; direct METI release was not retrieved in the bounded window.

news.headline: Taiwan plans tighter AI-chip and server export controls to China
facts: Bloomberg syndication said Economic Affairs Minister Kung Ming-hsin plans to add AI servers and cutting-edge semiconductors to controlled items.
Once effective, unauthorized restricted shipments to China could become criminal offenses under the Foreign Trade Act.
Kung did not give an implementation date.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Compliance and China-channel risk rise for chip distribution, server ODM and component suppliers; domestic advanced-node demand is not necessarily reduced. Enforcement details and product thresholds matter more than the headline.
news.uncertainty: This is a plan, not an effective rule. No implementation date or final official control list was verified. Yahoo/Bloomberg body extraction was rate-limited, so facts rely on checked search excerpts.

news.headline: Typhoon Champi could trigger warnings later this week
facts: CWA said a sea warning could come Wednesday night or Thursday morning and a land warning Thursday night or Friday.
As of Sunday 14:00, Champi was 2,470 km east-southeast of Eluanbi, moving west-northwest at 20 km/h with 191 km/h sustained winds and a 200 km storm radius.
Greatest potential impact was forecast for Friday/Saturday, with heavy rain possible in central, northern and eastern Taiwan.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Immediate market impact is limited Monday, but logistics, power continuity, construction and fab staffing plans should be monitored from Wednesday. Weather risk is operational, not yet a verified production disruption.
news.uncertainty: Track models were divergent at cutoff; no landfall was confirmed.

news.headline: TSMC posted record Q3 profit but stayed prudent on 2027
news.source_date: 2026-10-15; included as recent context, not overnight
facts: Q3 net profit rose 69% year-on-year to NT$763.1bn, beating the NT$746.3bn LSEG SmartEstimate.
TSMC raised 2026 revenue-growth expectation to about 44% and guided Q4 revenue to US$52.3bn-US$54.3bn.
It kept 2026 capex at US$60bn-US$64bn and said AI demand was extremely robust while expressing caution on 2027 macro uncertainty.
news.taiwan_mapping_inference: Fundamental demand remains strong, but the market is now testing valuation and financing assumptions across the AI chain; strong TSMC execution does not immunize suppliers from multiple compression.
news.uncertainty: Earlier than the weekend window; retained only to frame Monday's Taiwan reaction.

reader_suggestions.suggestion: Lead the brief with the cross-asset split: bonds and gold firmer, AI equities weaker, BTC/ETH bouncing but ETH/BTC lower. Call it defensive rotation plus crypto relative weakness, not a uniform risk-off move.

For Taiwan's open, watch whether TSMC/AI supply-chain selling confirms the US semiconductor impulse or whether lower yields produce an intraday stabilization. Separate strong TSMC fundamentals from sector multiple compression.

Use the Friday Farside figures as dated flow evidence: BTC -US$82.4m, ETH -US$69.7m; add weekly totals only as arithmetic. Emphasize ETH's larger weekly outflow and falling ETH/BTC without claiming causality.
Label WGC gold ETF data as through 2026-10-09: +US$627.6m and +4.485t globally. State that the week ending Oct. 16 was not available at the 09:30 cutoff.
Keep Champi as an operational watch item: no Monday disruption claim; reassess track, warnings, power/logistics and fab staffing from Tuesday night onward.
Key validation levels for subsequent updates: US 10Y around 5.05%, gold around US$4,180-4,200, BTC US$80,000/82,500 and ETH/BTC near 0.029. These are monitoring references, not trade instructions.
